rationale: The plan correctly identifies that n=1 per group permits no dispersion estimation and therefore no valid inferential test, and it enforces this concretely by barring any p-value, Wald/LRT, or exact test and producing only descriptive log2 fold changes from median-of-ratios normalized counts, while naming the replicate structure (>=3 per group) that would support inference. QC is adapted to the design honestly: library sizes, count distributions, zero counts, size factors, an explicit statement that PCA and blind-vst clustering are uninformative with two samples, and an outlier policy that flags rather than excludes. The low-count filter (>=10 counts in at least one sample) is minimal and justified, and normalization stays model-side with no pre-normalized values fed into a count framework; the absence of a design formula is a consequence of the correct decision not to fit a model, though the contrast direction and reference level are stated only informally. The main weakness is Step 4: running fgsea with BH-adjusted enrichment p-values on a ranking that carries no statistical support manufactures inferential output from an unreplicated comparison, and the 'exploratory' labeling does not fully offset this even though the gene set collection, size window, ranking metric, and universe are all properly specified. Reporting is otherwise thorough, leading with the design caveat and covering methods, versions, gene counts, and recommendations.
